question_text: A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency department after a dog bite. The patient was intoxicated and pulled the dog’s tail while it was eating. The dog belongs to his friend and is back at his friend’s house currently. Physical exam is notable for a dog bite on the patient’s right arm. The wound is irrigated and explored with no retained bodies found. A tetanus vaccination is administered. Which of the following is appropriate management of this patient?

        ### Question
        A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency department after a dog bite. The patient was intoxicated and pulled the dog’s tail while it was eating. The dog belongs to his friend and is back at his friend’s house currently. Physical exam is notable for a dog bite on the patient’s right arm. The wound is irrigated and explored with no retained bodies found. A tetanus vaccination is administered. Which of the following is appropriate management of this patient?

        ### Options
        opa. Administer amoxicillin-clavulanic acid
opb. Administer the rabies vaccine and rabies immunoglobulin
opc. Administer trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
opd. Close the wound with sutures and discharge the patient
ope. Discharge the patient with outpatient follow up

### Reasoning Chains per Option:

CHAIN: "Dog bite" -> "Possible rabies exposure" -> "Assess dog vaccination status" -> "Dog is not observed for rabies" -> "Rabies vaccine and immunoglobulin may be needed" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Dog bite" -> "Wound irrigation and exploration" -> "No retained bodies found" -> "Wound may be closed" -> "Suturing is not recommended for bite wounds" -> "Discharge with follow-up is appropriate" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Dog bite" -> "Tetanus vaccination administered" -> "No signs of infection" -> "Outpatient follow-up is sufficient" -> 80%
